name: BHUTAN
lead: Bhutan is a small kingdom in the Himalayas, between India and China. Its people call it Druk Yul, the Land of the Thunder Dragon. Bhutan measures success by happiness, not just money.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Bhutan is almost all mountains. In the north, icy Himalayan peaks rise above 7,000 m. In the warm south, jungle grows in the valleys. Three rivers carve deep gorges.
About 72% of Bhutan is covered in trees. Its forests take in more carbon dioxide (a gas that warms the Earth) than the country makes. So Bhutan is officially carbon-negative.
animals: Bhutan's national animal is the takin. It looks like a cow's body with a goat's head. Legend says a Buddhist saint made it from a cow and a goat at a feast.
Snow leopards prowl the high peaks. Red pandas curl up in bamboo forests. Black-necked cranes spend each winter in Phobjikha Valley.
culture: Bhutan measures wellbeing by Gross National Happiness. It balances the economy, nature, culture, and good government. Archery is the national sport. Matches are loud festivals with music and dancing.
Men wear a robe called a gho. Women wear a dress called a kira. People eat red rice and ema datshi (chilli and cheese) every day.
history: In the 1600s, the monk-warrior Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal unified Bhutan. He built huge forts called dzongs to guard each valley. Bhutan was never colonised (ruled by another country).
Bhutan became a constitutional democracy in 2008. Tourism opened in 1974, with strict limits to protect culture and forests.
wows: Bhutan's forests soak up more CO₂ than the country makes.
Climbing Gangkhar Puesum, the tallest unclimbed peak on Earth, is banned.
TV and internet both switched on the same day in 1999.
Gross National Happiness is part of Bhutan's constitution.
Thimphu is the only capital in the world with no traffic lights.
Tigers have been photographed at 4,000 m, higher than almost anywhere.
A law says buildings must follow traditional design, so there are no glass towers.

myths.fact: Everest is on the Nepal-China border. It is 8,849 m tall. All of Bhutan's peaks are lower.

myths.myth: Red pandas are cousins of giant pandas
myths.fact: Red pandas are not close kin to giant pandas. Their own family is closer to raccoons and weasels.
